developments.title: BoE tightening expectations leave sterling exposed to a less aggressive delivered path
developments.facts: Reuters reports LSEG money markets fully pricing four 25 bp BoE hikes by next September. ING expects a November increase and a likely February follow-up but describes the market curve as extreme. developments.facts: UK October final manufacturing PMI was 52.8, matching flash and above September 51.9; output rose to 53.6 and orders strengthened, while hiring stalled and input-cost inflation accelerated. developments.title: UK household borrowing slows; stronger business lending offsets the downside
developments.facts: September net house-purchase mortgage approvals fell to 53,400 from revised August 54,800; remortgage approvals rose to 42,600 from 34,000. Net mortgage borrowing slowed to GBP3.9bn from revised GBP4.2bn, below the prior six-month GBP4.9bn average. Net consumer credit fell to GBP1.9bn from revised GBP2.7bn, slightly below the prior six-month GBP2.1bn average. Mortgage borrowing and consumer credit were below broker forecasts GBP5.363bn and GBP2.368bn; approvals exceeded the broker forecast 50.828k but were slightly below the separately attributed web survey 54.00k. Do not call approvals an unqualified surprise miss. New mortgage effective rates rose to 4.63% from 4.60%. Offsetting household softness, non-financial business bank borrowing rose to GBP9.3bn from GBP4.7bn, M4Lex net flow rose to GBP17.0bn from GBP9.9bn and PNFC bank loans to GBP10.6bn from GBP6.4bn. PNFC total net finance nevertheless slowed to GBP3.1bn from GBP8.5bn after redemptions/buybacks. M4ex money net flow slowed to GBP3.9bn from GBP16.9bn. Levels, net flows and annual growth are distinct; this is one release package, not independent votes. September observations predate the October 28 budget and do not measure its effect.

developments.facts: The official October outlook describes a negative energy terms-of-trade shock. Central growth is around 1.25% in 2026 and 1% in 2027; 2027 is about half a percentage point below March. It projects CPI around 3.5% in 2027 and lower real disposable income than previously forecast. Fiscal consolidation is delayed, but the 2029-30 current-budget rule retains a GBP 15 billion margin. These are conditional forecasts. Fiscal margin, investment measures and a possible BoE inflation response are substantive opposition to GBP weakness. Additional directly opened post-delivery J.P. Morgan analysis says the budget met fiscal-restraint expectations, gilts slightly outperformed peers and sterling received modest support. It reports substantial expected BoE tightening but no new BoE commitment. The delivered reassurance challenges using structural growth/fiscal headwinds alone as the current-session direction.

developments.facts: ONS October 21 release reports September headline CPI 3.5% y/y versus 3.1% in August, core CPI 2.8% versus 2.6%, and CPI services 3.7% versus 3.4%. These are original October 21 observations that were available before the October 29 credit call, not newly released facts, evidence of new October 29 rate repricing or a guaranteed future hike.
